title: Sufficient grace given even to those who fail
source_text: XXVII. Gratiam quae ea ratione sufficiat ad bene operandum, dari contendunt illis ipsis qui reapse a bono opere deficiunt. Nempe quia Deus dat illis auxilia, per quae bene agere possint, quaeque subministrant eis potentiam proximam & completam bene operandi, scilicet, ut loquuntur Scholae, in actu primo: etsi desit illis aliud auxilium, quod praeexigitur ad ipsum bonum opus, quodque omnes quibus datur infallibiliter ad tale opus movet, & benigne etiam conceditur omnibus illis qui actu bene operantur. Qui propterea dicuntur habere gratiam ad bene agendum, non solum sufficientem, sed etiam efficacem.
pass_a_gloss: XXVII. Grace which in that way suffices for working well, they contend is given to those very ones who really fall short of the good work. Namely because God gives them helps, through which they can act well, and which supply them with the proximate and complete power of working well, namely, as the Schools speak, in first act: although there is lacking to them another help, which is prerequired for the good work itself, and which infallibly moves all to whom it is given to such work, and kindly also is granted to all those who in act work well. Who therefore are said to have grace for acting well, not only sufficient, but also efficacious.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXVII. They maintain that grace sufficient for doing good in this sense is given even to those who in fact fail to do the good work. God gives them aids by which they are able to act well, aids that furnish them proximate and complete power to do good, 'in first act', as the Schools put it.

What they lack is a further aid, required beforehand for the good work itself, which infallibly moves everyone who receives it to that work, and which God graciously grants to all who actually do good. These, accordingly, are said to have grace for doing good that is not only sufficient but efficacious too.

choices.term: in actu primo ... ad actum secundum
choices.why: Scholastic pair: first act is a power ready to act; second act is the operation itself (XXVII-XXIX).
